title: Nightwatch release observability notebook
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for a quieter, telemetry-first canary approach. Focus is to make flips low-friction for infra + client SDK teams while preserving SLOs and an easy pin/unpin story.

Context notes (why this exists):
- We've seen noisy rollouts where client traffic patterns (long prompt chains) expose long-tail latency and token cost spikes.
- Want a middle ground between full canary and shadowing: synthetic-driven cohort + tiny real-client fraction + rapid pin-back.
- This is intentionally messy — personal lab notes.

Key heuristics (first pass):
- Canary cohorts: tiny (0.2% - 2%) across 3 dimensions: client-tier, region, request-shape (short vs long).
- Synthetic probes: continuous low-rate probes that mimic 3 heavy prompt archetypes (LLM-ops, multi-turn chat, long-context completions).
- Warmup buckets: maintain a warmed KV cache per model-variant; ensure synthetic path hits same code-paths as real requests (same token lengths, same prompt prefixes).
- Pin semantics: pin at tenant level (prefer) or global fallback: pin -> immediate SDK flag flips to previous model + warmup trigger.

Telemetry & alerting primitives to wire up:
- Primary signals: p50/p95/p99 latency (inference-only), token cost per request, error-rate by error-class, model-compat mismatch errors.
- Synthetic health summary: rolling 30m, 3h, 24h views. If synthetic p95 increases >20% vs baseline -> start escalation.
- Canary delta rule: if real-client p95 delta > 15% and synthetic confirms trend -> auto-pin candidate.
- Safety multiplier for small cohorts: treat noisy metrics carefully (use Bayesian smoothing / min-sample thresholds).

Operational playbook snippets (quick scriptable steps):
- Preflight checklist (manual / automated):
  1) Confirm model artifact is in model-catalog with quant/code path metadata.
  2) Reserve warmup pool nodes for N minutes (ish: 10-30m depending on sequence lengths).
  3) Start synthetic probes against model-variant and capture KV cache hit-rate.
  4) Deploy canary routing rule (0.2% initial) with circuit-breaker TTL 5m.
  5) Watch synthetic + cohort telemetry for 30m before increasing fraction.

- Rapid pin/unpin script (notes):
  - SDK toggle: route clients with header X-RW-Model=stable -> old model. Implement server-side toggle that overrides per-tenant routing for N minutes.
  - Version pin: record pin event with reason, operator, and auto-unpin window (if set). Pin must trigger a background warmup to reduce cold-start variance on rollback.

Questions / unknowns to follow up on:
- Do we want an "escape hatch" that warm-starts a compatible smaller quantized variant automatically when p99 spikes? (pros: cheaper, keeps service; cons: quality regressions).
- What's an acceptable TTL for automatic unpin? 1h, 24h, indefinite? Need product input + client consent map.
- How to make synthetic probes faithful for multi-tenant prompt distributions (we risk probing wrong distribution and missing real-client regressions).

Hypotheses to test (experiments):
- H1: Synthetic heavy-chat probes will find regressions faster than tiny real-cohort because synthetic coverage of long sequences increases signal-to-noise.
  - Experiment: run synthetic-only vs synthetic+0.5% cohort side-by-side and measure median time-to-detect under injected latency faults.
- H2: Warmup of KV cache across 2 minutes reduces p99 of first-third requests by >30% for long sequences.
  - Experiment: variable warmup durations (0, 2, 10 mins) and synthetic replay for each window.

Instrumentation snippets (metrics I want):
- metric.inference.latency_ms:labels(model_variant, region, cohort, request_shape)
- metric.kvcache.hit_rate:labels(model_variant, region)
- metric.synthetic.success_rate:labels(probe_type, model_variant)
- trace:warmup:labels(model_variant, node_pool) -> count/latency of warmup requests

Rollback heuristics (practical):
- Immediate pin triggers when: error-rate spike > 1% absolute AND p95 latency increase > 30% sustained for 3 consecutive 5m windows (and synthetic confirms).
- Soft pin: reduce cohort fraction by 75% and extend circuit-breaker window to 15m; observe for 30m. If still bad -> hard pin.

Notes on client UX and SDK behaviour:
- Prefer server-side override + ephemeral per-tenant pin metadata so SDK doesn't need immediate rollout; SDK only polls pin metadata on heartbeat. Example header flow: X-RW-Pin:tenant-id=abc;model=stable;reason=latency-spike;operator=oliver
- For progressive rollout, add a per-tenant warmup flag so large tenants get a longer ramp.

Edge-cases to document for runbook:
- Region-specific infra blips (cloud provider AZ outage) vs model regressions -> need region-isolation before pin.
- Cache thrash: many small clients with unique prefixes can evict warm caches -> synthetic should emulate multi-prefix churn.
- Multi-model fallbacks: if fallback is not quality-equivalent, tie a quality-eval gate before automatic fallback.

Quick TODO (actionable):
- [ ] Add probe templates for 3 archetypes to synthetic harness (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Wire metric.inference.latency with cohort labels (owner: me).
- [ ] Draft product note re: auto-unpin policies and client consent (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Bake a small CLI that executes the soft-pin sequence (preflight checks, set pin meta, kickwarmup) (owner: me).

Loose thoughts / heuristics (brain-dump):
- Make pins first-class events in audit logs and surface them in Console with a one-click rollback.
- Prefer observability over larger canary fractions; more coverage of request-shapes is often better than bigger sample size.
- Keep a quick ledger of "why pins happened" by tenant so we can correlate to client-reported regressions.

Unresolved personal notes:
- Would like to prototype an "adaptive probe" that increases synthetic probe intensity on metric drift. Probably a control-theory problem; low-priority.
- Consider a 'quiet-hour' window where releases default to more conservative heuristics (e.g., 00:00-06:00 PST).

Slack refs / quick links (internal):
- slack: #infra-rollouts thread (search "nightwatch")
- TODO: link to runbook page once finalized: confluence:release-runbook-2026

If time permits: convert this to a short checklist that on-call can run in 5 minutes and a separate one-pager for PMs about auto-unpin tradeoffs.

-- oliver
